prompt: Map click pixels to board cells: complete cellAt (bounds first, then divide -- Java truncates towards zero) and a mouseClicked handler that toggles the cell it lands on.
explanation: Hit-testing is the bridge between pixel coordinates and whatever the program actually models, and it is almost always subtract-origin then divide-by-size. The bounds test has to come first because integer division truncates towards zero: (5 - 10) / 25 is 0, so a point five pixels left of the board would be reported as column 0. Using a half-open range -- x from LEFT up to but not including LEFT + COLS * CELL -- makes neighbouring cells tile without overlapping.
hints: Reject out-of-range x and y first, returning "none", and only then compute (x - LEFT) / CELL and (y - TOP) / CELL.
The board ends just before LEFT + COLS * CELL, so use >= for the far edge test, not >.
In mouseClicked, call your own cellAt and only toggle when the result is not "none"; splitting the string at the comma gives you the row and column.
